record.paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
record.context_brief: Minimal order for one real and one complex pole pair
record.original_question: For phase-type distributions with Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=1/q(s), where q(s)=(1+s/c)(1+s/(a+ib))(1+s/(a-ib)) and a,b,c are positive real parameters, suppose the eigenvalue-angle condition for phase-type generators gives a lower bound n_min on the possible order of any representation. Does there always exist a phase-type representation of exactly order n_min for every such distribution?

evidence.quote: Consider a PH-distribution with Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=1/q(s), q(s)=(1+s/c)(1+s/(a+ib))(1+s/(a-ib)) where a, b, c > 0.
For PH-distributions with Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=1/q(s) where q(s) is as in (42), Theorem 6 gives a minimal order nmin for a representation.
Conjecture 1: There exists a representation of order nmin for such a distribution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A continuous phase-type (PH) distribution is the distribution of the absorption time of a continuous-time Markov chain on the state space {1,...,n,n+1}, where state n+1 is absorbing and states 1,...,n are transient. Such a distribution is characterized by a pair (α, T), called a representation of order n, where α is a 1×n nonnegative row vector with α·1 ≤ 1 (the initial distribution on transient states) and T is an n×n sub-generator matrix (off-diagonal entries nonnegative, row sums ≤ 0, T nonsingular). Its Laplace–Stieltjes transform is f̃(s) = α(sI − T)^{-1}(−T)·1.

The order of a PH distribution is the smallest n for which it admits such a representation. A classical necessary condition (O'Cinneide's eigenvalue/angle condition) on the eigenvalues of T provides, for any given PH distribution, a lower bound n_min on the order of any phase-type representation of it.

Consider the family of PH distributions whose Laplace transforms have the form
   f̃(s) = 1 / q(s),    q(s) = (1 + s/c)(1 + s/(a+ib))(1 + s/(a−ib)),
with parameters a, b, c > 0 (so q has one real pole −c and a complex-conjugate pair of poles −a ± ib), under the assumption that f̃ is indeed the Laplace transform of some PH distribution. Let n_min denote the lower bound on the order coming from the eigenvalue/angle condition applied to such a distribution.

Question: Does every such PH distribution admit a phase-type representation of order exactly n_min?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search confirms that determining the minimal order of phase-type distributions whose Laplace transform denominators have complex-conjugate poles is a well-known hard problem, where the minimal order can substantially exceed the algebraic degree (O'Cinneide). No source found that conclusively confirms or refutes the specific conjecture that the eigenvalue/angle lower bound n_min is always attainable in the one-real-pole plus one-complex-pair case. Status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Order of Phase-Type Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: The size of a minimal irreducible representation of a PH distribution is referred to as its order; O'Cinneide showed the order may be greater than the algebraic degree.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the minimal order beyond the algebraic-degree lower bound is generally an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Algebraic Degree of Phase-Type Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: When the denominator polynomial has non-real roots, the minimal PH representation problem becomes much more complicated and the order can be dramatically larger than the algebraic degree.
status_evidence.claim: The complex-pole case is recognized as substantially harder and is not fully resolved.
